label: prf:borromean-h4-categorical-derivation
title: Proof of borromean h4 categorical derivation
html:
Proof. Proof of borromean h4 categorical derivation

Proof.

The proof proceeds in two structural steps.

Step 1 — Schur–Weyl + R-matrix derivation of \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}).

The q-Schur duality for \mathrm{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) and \mathrm{H}_3(q) gives a (\mathrm{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), \mathrm{H}_3(q))-bimodule decomposition

  V_{1/2}^{\otimes 3}
  \;\cong\;
  V_{3/2} \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  V_{1/2} \otimes S^{(2,1)}

(dimensions: 4 \otimes 1 \;\oplus\; 2 \otimes 2 \;=\; 4 + 4 = 8). Tracing on the V^{\otimes 3} side via the standard ordinary trace (matching the \mathrm{H}_n(q)-side classical-dim convention) gives:

  \mathrm{tr}_{V^{\otimes 3}}(F(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}))
  \;=\;
  \dim(V_{3/2}) \cdot \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;+\;
  \dim(V_{1/2}) \cdot \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  4 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}),

where F is the q-Schur duality functor sending the braid generators \sigma_i to the braided R-matrices \check{R}_{i, i+1} acting on V_{1/2}^{\otimes 3}, and \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1 since \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} has writhe 0 and projects to the identity in S_3.

The braided R-matrix is

  \check{R}(q) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
    0 & q - q^{-1} & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\
    0 & 0 & 0 & q
  \end{pmatrix}

in the basis \{|\!\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle, |\!\!\uparrow\downarrow\rangle, |\!\!\downarrow\uparrow\rangle, |\!\!\downarrow\downarrow\rangle\}, satisfying the Hecke relation (\check{R} - q)(\check{R} + q^{-1}) = 0. Its inverse is

  \check{R}^{-1} \;=\; \check{R} - (q - q^{-1}) I,

derived from the Hecke quadratic relation \check{R}^2 = (q - q^{-1})\check{R} + I (this is not \check{R}(q \to q^{-1}), which is the universal R-matrix not the braided form). Setting \sigma_1 = \check{R} \otimes I_2, \sigma_2 = I_2 \otimes \check{R} as 8 \times 8 matrices on V^{\otimes 3}, direct computation of \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2)^3 gives:

  \mathrm{tr}_{V^{\otimes 3}}(F(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}))
  \;=\;
  8 - 6h^4 - 2h^6
  \quad\text{(exact, verified to 50 digits at the substrate $q_0 \approx 1.10998$).}

Subtracting 4 \cdot 1 and dividing by \dim(V_{1/2}) = 2 yields:

  \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  2 - 3h^4 - h^6,

i.e. the h^4 coefficient is -3. (This polynomial form is also derivable directly from the closed form of prop:borromean-markov-trace-closed-form via the substitution u = q^2 + q^{-2} = h^2 + 2; the R-matrix derivation provides the categorical confirmation.)

Step 2 — Markov normalisation y_{(2,1)}(q=1) = 1/[2]_q^2|_{q=1} = 1/4.

The Frobenius expansion of the Markov trace on \mathrm{H}_3(q):

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} y_\lambda(q) \cdot \chi^\lambda(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  y_{(3)}(q) + y_{(2,1)}(q)\!\cdot\!(2 - 3h^4 - h^6) + y_{(1^3)}(q),

using \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = \chi^{(1^3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1. Regrouping:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{\bigl[y_{(3)} + 2\, y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}\bigr]}_{= \,\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}_3) \,=\, 1 \text{ (Markov norm.)}}
  \;+\;
  y_{(2,1)}(q) \cdot (-3h^4 - h^6),

since the Markov normalisation gives \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \cdot d_\lambda = \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}_3) = 1 for the identity braid. The h^4 coefficient is therefore

  \bigl[h^4\text{-coeff of }\mathrm{tr}_M\bigr] \;=\; -3 \cdot y_{(2,1)}(q=1).

From the closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6) / (h^2 + 4) the h^4 coefficient is -3/4 (exact symbolic series division). Solving:

  -3 \cdot y_{(2,1)}(q=1) \;=\; -\tfrac{3}{4}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  y_{(2,1)}(q=1) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{4} \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q^2|_{q=1}}.

The factor [2]_q^{c-1} is the standard Markov-trace normalisation for closure of an n-strand braid into a c-component link: for the Borromean rings (c = 3), [2]_q^2 = h^2 + 4 is exactly the denominator in the closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (\cdots)/(h^2 + 4).

The identity y_{(2,1)}(q) = 1/[2]_q^2 in fact holds exactly for all q, not only at q = 1: the full closed-form weight vector on \mathrm{H}_3(q) is y_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3, y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2, y_{(1^3)} = 0 (identically — the Temperley–Lieb quotient kills the 3-row partition), evaluating at q = 1 to the non-uniform vector (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0). See prop:h3-markov-wenzl-weights for the derivation and for why a bar-involution uniformity argument fails (the Jones-normalised trace is chiral — not invariant under the sign-twist automorphism \sigma \mapsto -q\,\sigma^{-1}).

Combining Steps 1 and 2.

  \bigl[h^4\text{-coeff of }\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})\bigr]
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{(-3)}_{\text{Step 1: R-matrix on }V_{1/2}^{\otimes 3}}
  \;\cdot\;
  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{4}}_{\text{Step 2: Markov norm. for }c = 3}
  \;=\;
  -\tfrac{3}{4}. \qquad \square
